quote: [Section 3.5 preamble:] In the area of reliability and survival analysis, various stochastic orderings between two random variables have been considered. The following theorem gives the conditions under which CLFRD preserves likelihood ratio ordering. A random variable X is said to be larger than another random variable Y in likelihood ratio order (written as X ≥LR Y) if for all x ≥ 0, gX(x)/gY(x) is increasing in x. Theorem 3.2. Let X and Y be two random variables following CLFRD with parameters α1, β1, λ1 and α2, β2, λ2 respectively, then X ≥LR (≤LR) Y provided (i) α1 ≤ (≥) α2; (ii) β1 ≤ (≥) β2; (iii) λ1 ≤ (≥) λ2.
family: Compounded linear failure rate distribution CLFRD(α, β, λ): survival Ḡ(x) = P(U ≥ x) = exp(−αx − (β/2)x² − λ + λ exp(−αx − (β/2)x²)), x ≥ 0, α, β, λ > 0 (eq. (1)); pdf g(x) = (α + βx)[1 + λ exp(−αx − (β/2)x²)] / exp(αx + (β/2)x² + λ − λ exp(−αx − (β/2)x²)) (eq. (3)); arises as U = min{X1, ..., XN}, Xi iid LFRD(α, β), N − 1 ~ Poisson(λ)
